title: Operator workflow acceleration: tooling catalog & adoption playbook
author: Priya Shah
body:
Summary:

This document catalogs the set of platform operator tooling that the eng-platform team endorses for accelerating operator workflows, reduces cognitive load during incidents, and improves MTTR for LLM inference services. It also gives a recommended adoption playbook, runbook snippets, dashboard templates, and measured success criteria. The goal is to standardize operator tooling across regions and reduce bespoke scripts and ad-hoc consoles.

Background and motivation:

Over 2025 we observed recurring patterns where operators spent 40–60% of incident time on low-value tasks: cross-region context gathering, tenant debit reconciliation, and manual KV-cache shard rebalancing. Several pockets of automation were introduced ad-hoc, but lack of a curated, supported catalog slowed uptake and caused duplication. This catalog is the first-team curated offering to accelerate workflows while preserving operator autonomy.

Scope:

- Included: operator-facing CLI tools, web UIs, lightweight agent helpers, dashboard templates, and runbook snippets that integrate with our runtime and telemetry.
- Excluded: customer-facing consoles, vendor-only closed-source tools that cannot be audited by engineering.

Principles for inclusion:

1. Observable: every tool must emit standardized telemetry (tool.name, tool.action, request_id) to telemetry.ingest.platform-tools.
2. Reversible: actions that modify runtime state must be reversible or provide an automated rollback within 5 minutes.
3. ACL-aware: use RBAC hooks in platform-authz; no tool bypasses tenant isolation checks.
4. Test-first: every tool must have a synthetic /test endpoint and a canary release in a staging region.

Catalog (short descriptions and recommended owners):

- op-inspect (CLI) — a single-command cross-region context aggregator. Pulls traces, last 50 requests, and cost meters for a given tenant. Owner: platform-telemetry. Use-case: fast context during oncall.
- kv-shard-rebalancer (service) — orchestrated KV cache shard resharding with quiesce windows and preflight checks. Owner: serving-runtime. Safety: automatic 1% traffic probe; rollback on >5% SLI delta.
- tenant-credit-visualizer (dashboard template) — Grafana dashboard showing spend velocity, credit buffer, and forecasted 24h expiry. Owner: billing-integrations. Tag: billing.
- quick-swap-model (operator UI) — safe model variant swap with pre-checks for embedding dimension and tokenizer compatibility. Owner: model-onboarding. Gate: require model-compatibility check pass.
- operator-safe-mode (operator-runbook service) — atomic degrade mode toggles (graded degradation). Owner: eng-platform-runbooks. SLA: action replication under 2s to regional controllers.
- batch-prioritizer (agent) — local operator utility to test tenant priority weighting in a dry-run mode against the scheduler. Owner: allocator-team.
- prefetch-simulator (lab tool) — synthetic workload generator to validate prefetch and warmset heuristics. Owner: performance-lab.

Each entry above must reference an internal component name and the owning pager. See appendix A for contact matrix.

Runbook snippets (copyable) — common operator flows:

1) Incident triage: long tail token latency spike

- Step 1: Run op-inspect --tenant <tenant-id> --window 15m; gather top-3 endpoints and model variants.
- Step 2: Open tenant-credit-visualizer for tenant-id to rule out credit-driven throttles.
- Step 3: If KV cache miss rate > 8% and tail P99 latency >= 1.5x baseline, invoke kv-shard-rebalancer --dry-run.
- Step 4: If operator-safe-mode recommended_degrade == true, follow graded-degrade checklist (2a: alert customers, 2b: enable fallback variants).

2) Planned model rollout (operator-assisted canary)

- Step 1: Create rollout in rollout-dsl with canary 5% traffic and health checks: model_diff_embedding_cosine < 0.03 and error_rate < 0.1%.
- Step 2: Use quick-swap-model UI to stage variant; run prefetch-simulator against canary cohort.
- Step 3: After 60m stable, increment canary to 25% and monitor llm-quality-regression SLI.
- Step 4: Full rollout must hit metrics for 48h before closing the rollout.

Operator dashboard templates and alerting guidance:

We publish three Grafana templates in dashboards/team/operator-templates that must be installed per-region:

- Operator overview (compact): tenant error heatmap, region capacity usage, operator-queue-latency, token cost velocity.
- Failure triage (wide): per-model P95/P99, KV cache miss rate, scheduler-queue-depth by priority, prefetch hit ratio.
- Degradation simulator (synthetic): runs prefetch-simulator output vs expected warmset curves.

Alerting thresholds (recommended starting values):

- operator-queue-latency.p95 > 500ms for 5m -> P1 candidate (investigate backlog and prefetch).
- kv-cache.miss_rate > 8% -> P2 (consider reshard).
- model-variant.error_rate > 0.2% -> P1 if sustained >10m or customer-facing SLA impacted.
- token-cost.velocity > forecasted + 30% for 10m -> P2 (billing ops loop-in).

Each alert must include runbook link and op-inspect command prefilled in the alert annotation. Alerts are stored under alerts/operator/.

Adoption playbook (3-phase):

Phase 0 — discovery (2 weeks): inventory existing operator scripts, map owners, and run the adoption readiness checklist.
Phase 1 — pilot (4–8 weeks): onboard 3 regional oncall teams; install operator-templates dashboards, require synthetic-run passes, and collect feedback.
Phase 2 — org-wide rollout (6–12 weeks): mandatory install for all operators, deprecation schedule for legacy scripts (90-day sunset), and training sessions.

Training and enablement:

- 2-hour hands-on lab: scenario-driven (triage, model swap, reshard).
- Certification: operator-tooling-basic badge after completing checklist and passing a simulated run (45-minute supervised lab).
- Office hours: weekly for first 12 weeks of rollout.

Metrics of success (what we measure):

- MTTR reduction: target 25% reduction in median MTTR for P1 incidents related to inference (baseline: 48m).
- Tool usage: op-inspect executed by at least 80% of shift leads during incidents within 3 months.
- Runbook fidelity: <10% of incidents require ad-hoc scripts beyond catalog within 6 months.
- Regression incidence: no increase in customer-facing quality regressions attributable to tooling rollout.

Risk and mitigations:

- Risk: operator over-reliance on automation causing unnoticed regressions. Mitigation: safety gates, mandatory dry-run, and synthetic checks before state changes.
- Risk: tools introduce new telemetry costs. Mitigation: sample tool telemetry at 10% for high-frequency actions and provide aggregated summaries.
- Risk: inconsistent installs across regions. Mitigation: orchestration job (infra-owner) to validate installation weekly and alert on drift.

Ownership and support model:

- Platform-telemetry: op-inspect support and instrumentation (pager: @platform-telemetry-pager).
- Serving-runtime: kv-shard-rebalancer (pager: @serving-runtime-pager).
- Eng-platform-runbooks: operator-safe-mode orchestration and documentation.
- Platform-ops: rollout orchestration and onboarding schedule.

Roadmap (12 months):

- Q1: finalize catalog APIs and add RBAC integration for quick-swap-model.
- Q2: automate dashboard installation via infra delivery pipeline and run first operator certification cohort.
- Q3: integrate tooling telemetry into operator-sentiment metrics and begin MTTR cohort analysis.
- Q4: deprecate top-3 legacy scripts and publish post-rollout retrospective.

Appendix A — contact matrix (copyable):

- platform-telemetry: priya.shah@redwood.ai, pager: @platform-telemetry-pager
- serving-runtime: diego.ramos@redwood.ai, pager: @serving-runtime-pager
- allocator-team: ethan.morales@redwood.ai
- model-onboarding: sofia.liang@redwood.ai

Appendix B — sample CLI command examples:

- op-inspect quick usage: op-inspect --tenant tenant-123 --window 15m --output json | jq .summary
- kv-shard-rebalancer dry-run: kv-shard-rebalancer --shard s-42 --strategy evenize --dry-run --safety-window 10m

Appendix C — installation checklist (to be completed per-region before pilot):

1) Install op-inspect v1.2.0 or later and grant role: operator/basic.
2) Install grafana templates from dashboards/team/operator-templates and verify data sources.
3) Deploy prefetch-simulator in lab namespace and run smoke test.
4) Configure alert annotations with runbook links and sample op-inspect commands.

Notes and next steps:

- Submit pilot candidate regions to platform-ops by 2026-01-31.
- Owners should schedule cross-team tabletop run-through within two weeks of pilot start.
